The pre-rebase tip measures 4432 with an offender set identical to the merged tree's, so the commit that re-floored this gate to what the webhook extraction left behind banked the reduction and did not re-measure the growth beside it.

Measured with the CI command (py_function_length.py --count) on four trees, which is what makes the attribution a reading rather than a story:

  merge-base 300a155e269   4391   (its floor, 4391, reproduces)
  origin/19.0-marin        4391   (unchanged: none of its 35 commits touches an offender)
  this branch, pre-rebase  4432   (against a committed 4391)
  merged                   4432

Diffing the full offender lists (--top 0, 120 offenders each side) against origin gives the whole of the +41 in four functions, all of them this branch's ESM pipeline work and nothing else:

  odoo/tools/assets/esm_registry.py::_build                    99 -> 127   +28
  odoo/addons/base/models/ir_qweb_assets.py::_esm_prod_nodes  182 -> 190    +8
  odoo/addons/base/models/ir_qweb_assets.py::_esm_debug_nodes 198 -> 201    +3

_build carries 28 of the 41 because recording what a specifier maps TO, rather than that it is mapped, is a second table and the loop that fills it. That is the growth the change is for, and it is banked here rather than hidden: the extraction that would pay it back splits the registry's build from its resolution, which is a change to the ESM pipeline's shape and not a drive-by.
